- VPC with subnets pub-a, pub-b (public, AZ a/b), app-a, app-b (private application tier), db-a, db-b (private data tier).
- Internet gateway attached. Route tables: rt-pub (pub-a, pub-b): default route -> igw. rt-app-a (app-a): default -> nat-a.
  rt-app-b (app-b): default -> nat-b. rt-db (db-a, db-b): local only.
- NAT gateways nat-a in pub-a and nat-b in pub-b, each with an elastic IP.
- Network ACLs: nacl-pub (public subnets) allows all traffic in and out. nacl-app (app subnets): inbound tcp/80 from the VPC,
  inbound tcp/1024-65535 from anywhere; outbound all. nacl-db (db subnets): inbound tcp/3306 from app subnets; outbound tcp/1024-65535 to app subnets.
- Security groups: sg-alb inbound tcp/80 and tcp/443 from anywhere, outbound all. sg-app inbound tcp/80 from sg-alb, outbound all.
  sg-db inbound tcp/3306 from sg-app, outbound all. No security group allows ICMP.
- Internet-facing Application Load Balancer in pub-a and pub-b with sg-alb; listener :80 forwards to target group tg-app
  (port 80, health check GET /health expecting 200).
- Auto Scaling group across app-a and app-b, desired 2, attached to tg-app, ELB health checks, launch template:
  AMI ami-web-v3, instance profile role-app, sg-app, no public IP, web server on :80; user data fetches config/app.json from S3 at boot
  (the web server does not start if this fails).
- IAM role role-app (trusted by ec2.amazonaws.com): s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::assets-bkt/*,
  logs:PutLogEvents, Systems Manager agent permissions.
- Bucket assets-bkt: bucket policy grants CloudFront origin access control read access to static/; no deny statements.
- RDS MySQL, Multi-AZ, subnets db-a/db-b, sg-db. App config (in S3) holds DB endpoint appdb.current and the current password.
- CloudFront distribution: default origin = the ALB over HTTP (http-only); /static/* origin = assets-bkt via origin access control.

ACTIONS (one per turn)
Edge probes: alb_get_root (HTTP GET / directly on the ALB from the internet), ping_alb (ICMP echo to the ALB).
Service telemetry: target_health (tg-app target states and reason codes), asg_activity (Auto Scaling activity history),
  console_a / console_b (boot log of the instance in AZ a / b), read_app_logs (recent application errors in CloudWatch Logs),
  flow_logs (VPC flow-log summary at an application instance ENI: inbound health-check port, outbound tcp/443).
Instance shell via Session Manager (suffix @a or @b selects the instance): curl_localhost_health@a, curl_internet@a,
  ping_internet@a, nc_rds_3306@a, ping_rds@a, s3_put_test@a, sts_identity@a (same with @b).
Configuration inspection (shows the deployed settings): c_rt_pub, c_rt_app_a, c_rt_app_b, c_igw, c_nat_a, c_nat_b,
  c_nacl_pub, c_nacl_app, c_nacl_db, c_sg_alb, c_sg_app, c_sg_db, c_alb, c_tg, c_asg, c_lt, c_role, c_bucket, c_rds, c_appcfg, c_cf.

INCIDENT TICKET (synthetic monitors)
- GET https://site/ via CloudFront: 502 intermittent-503
- GET /items (database-backed page) via CloudFront: 502 intermittent-503
- POST /upload (stores a file in S3) via CloudFront: 502 intermittent-503
- GET /static/logo.png via CloudFront: 200
- Resilience test: AZ a taken offline: root=502 intermittent-503 items=502 intermittent-503
- Resilience test: AZ b taken offline: root=502 intermittent-503 items=502 intermittent-503
- CloudWatch alarm UnHealthyHostCount>0: ALARM
- Instances managed by Systems Manager: none
- Application log streams receiving events: no

{"action": "target_health"}

Result of target_health: a:unhealthy (Target.FailedHealthChecks);b:unhealthy (Target.FailedHealthChecks)
Turns left: 14

Both targets fail health checks, and the boot log will show whether the web server is starting at all, so I'll check the instance in AZ a.

{"action": "console_a"}

Result of console_a: fetch-config: connect timeout s3.amazonaws.com:443
Turns left: 13

The boot log shows the instance can't reach S3 on 443, so the web server never starts. That points at the instance's outbound path. The app subnets route through NAT, so I'll check the NAT-side route table for app-a.

{"action": "c_rt_app_a"}

Result of c_rt_app_a: ('rt-app-a', 'nat-a', ['app-a'])
Turns left: 12
{"action": "c_nat_a"}

Result of c_nat_a: ('nat-a', 'pub-a', True)
Turns left: 11
{"action": "c_nacl_app"}

Result of c_nacl_app: ('nacl-app', [(100, 'allow', 'tcp', 80, 80, 'vpc'), (110, 'allow', 'tcp', 1024, 65535, 'any')], [(100, 'allow', 'all', 0, 65535, 'any')])
Turns left: 10

The app-subnet NACL looks right: inbound tcp/80 from the VPC and ephemeral ports from anywhere, with all outbound allowed. The S3 connect timeout could still be a NACL or route problem on the public side, so I'll check the public NACL next.

{"action": "c_nacl_pub"}

Result of c_nacl_pub: ('nacl-pub', [(100, 'allow', 'all', 0, 65535, 'any')], [(100, 'allow', 'all', 0, 65535, 'any')])
Turns left: 9
{"action": "c_rt_pub"}

Result of c_rt_pub: ('rt-pub', 'igw', ['pub-a', 'pub-b'])
Turns left: 8
{"action": "c_igw"}

Result of c_igw: ('igw', 'attached')
Turns left: 7

The network path from app-a through NAT-a and the public subnets to the internet gateway checks out, so the fault is more likely at the S3 end or in the instance's identity. The instance profile's role is what grants S3 access, so I'll check that role next.

{"action": "c_role"}

Result of c_role: ('role', 'ec2.amazonaws.com', [('logs:PutLogEvents', '*'), ('s3:GetObject', 'arn:aws:s3:::assets-bkt/*'), ('s3:PutObject', 'arn:aws:s3:::assets-bkt/*'), ('ssm:UpdateInstanceInformation', '*')])
Turns left: 6

The role's S3 permissions match the design: GetObject and PutObject on assets-bkt, plus logs and SSM. A timeout on connecting to s3.amazonaws.com is a network failure, not an authorization one, so the role isn't the cause. The remaining suspect on this path is NAT-a itself, which I've already read as valid, so I'll test the instance's outbound connectivity directly.

{"action": "ping_internet@a"}

Result of ping_internet@a: session unavailable
Turns left: 5

Session Manager is unavailable on this instance. The "Instances managed by Systems Manager: none" line in the ticket explains that: the instance isn't registering with SSM, so the shell actions won't work. I'll check the security group on the app tier, since outbound traffic from the instance is filtered there.

{"action": "c_sg_app"}

Result of c_sg_app: ('sg-app', [('tcp', 80, 80, 'sg-alb')], [])
Turns left: 4

The sg-app outbound rule list is empty. Security groups deny all outbound traffic unless a rule allows it, so the instance can't reach S3 or anything else on 443. The design calls for outbound all, which would explain the connect timeout in the boot log and the failed health checks, since the instance never starts its web server.

{"diagnosis": {"resource": "sg-app", "misconfiguration": "The outbound rules on sg-app are empty, so the app instances cannot send any traffic, including the HTTPS call to S3 that user data needs at boot; the intended design allows all outbound."}}
Repair applied to sg-app. The incident is resolved.
